concepts.title: The Indian National Congress and the National Movement
concepts.definition: The Indian National Congress, founded in Bombay in 1885, became the main platform of the freedom struggle, moving from early moderate petitions to mass agitation as leaders and people joined hands against colonial rule.
concepts.key_idea: From petition to protest: the Congress turned elite demands into a people's movement.
concepts.textbook_ref: hees202.txt lines 58-100 (Indian National Congress in Bombay), 452-520 (rise of the national movement)
question_patterns: when and where was the Indian National Congress founded
how did the aims of the Congress change over time
distinguish moderates and extremists in the national movement
what role did the Congress play in the freedom struggle
name the early leaders of the Indian National Congress
why is 1885 a landmark year in Indian history

solution_steps.explain: Educated Indians met at Bombay in 1885 to form the Congress.
Moderate prayer-and-petition politics gave way to swadeshi and mass mobilisation.
Peasants, workers and women joined, making independence a national demand.

concepts.title: Purna Swaraj and the Mass Movements
concepts.definition: The demand crystallised as Purna Swaraj - complete independence - proclaimed in 1929-30; Gandhian movements of non-cooperation and civil disobedience, salt marches and boycotts drew millions into open defiance of British rule.
concepts.key_idea: Purna Swaraj turned the goal from dominion status to complete independence, fought with non-violent mass action.
question_patterns: what is meant by Purna Swaraj
when and where was the Purna Swaraj resolution passed
describe the salt satyagraha and its importance
what methods did Gandhiji use in the freedom struggle
how did ordinary people participate in civil disobedience
what was the impact of the naval mutiny of 1946

solution_steps.explain: The Lahore session of 1929 resolved that Purna Swaraj was the only aim.
Salt law breaking, boycotts and non-cooperation brought the masses to the streets.
Repression failed; mutinies like the Royal Indian Navy rising showed the empire losing loyalty.

concepts.title: Revolutionaries, Azad Hind and the Armed Challenge
concepts.definition: Alongside non-violence ran the armed stream - revolutionaries who fought and sacrificed - and Subhas Chandra Bose's Azad Hind movement, which proclaimed a provisional government and led the Indian National Army against the British during the Second World War.
concepts.key_idea: From underground revolutionaries to the Azad Hind Fauj, armed resistance complemented the mass movement.
concepts.textbook_ref: hees202.txt lines 149-220 (navy mutiny, Azad Hind proclaimed, royal proclamation)
question_patterns: who proclaimed Azad Hind and when

solution_steps.explain: Young militants resorted to arms against colonial officials and symbols.
Azad Hind government and the INA carried the fight to India's eastern frontier.
INA trials and mutinies stirred even the armed forces against the Raj.

concepts.title: Social Reform and the Awakening: Roy, Bankim and Syed Ahmad Khan
concepts.definition: The nineteenth-century awakening ran through reformers - Raja Ram Mohan Roy against sati and for modern education, Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay whose Vande Mataram stirred patriotism from the 1860s-70s, and Syed Ahmad Khan promoting education among Muslims - alongside movements like the Arya Samaj.
concepts.key_idea: Reformers fought social evils and spread education, preparing the soil of nationalism.
concepts.textbook_ref: hees202.txt lines 301-350 (Bankim Chandra, Syed Ahmad Khan, Raja Ram Mohan Roy, Arya Samaj)
question_patterns: what reforms did Raja Ram Mohan Roy champion
how did Vande Mataram inspire nationalists
what was the contribution of Syed Ahmad Khan
what were the aims of the Arya Samaj
how did social reform movements prepare the ground for independence
name two nineteenth century reformers and their work

solution_steps.explain: Roy fought social evils; Bankim's song lit patriotic feeling; Syed Ahmad urged education.
Brahmo Samaj and Arya Samaj attacked superstition and caste rigidity.
Reform created pride, unity and modern ideas that fed the freedom struggle.
